name: Lightreel
tagline: AI tool that turns prompts, scripts or product assets into short-form video.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Anything in this category is a thin app wrapped around video and voice models that nobody is running on a laptop. You can absolutely build the orchestration layer: script generation, shot list, clip fetch or generation, captions, music bed, render. What you cannot build is the generation itself, so your personal version is a billing account at somebody else's inference provider with a nicer UI on top. That is not a replacement, that is a different middleman, and it will cost you roughly what the product costs once you are paying per second of video. The honest DIY win is a deterministic template renderer where you supply the footage yourself, which is a real tool but a different product.
coreLoopDIY: A local CLI that takes a script, generates voiceover and captions, stitches your own supplied clips or stock footage to the audio timing, and renders a vertical MP4.
requirements: An LLM API key for script and shot list generation
A TTS API key, or a local TTS model if you want zero cloud
Your own footage, or a stock video API key
Patience for font, caption timing and aspect ratio bikeshedding
whatYouLose: Actual generative video: no text-to-clip, no avatars, no lipsync
Model upgrades happening without you doing anything
Templates that already look like they belong on a feed instead of like a school project
Browser-based editing, previews and re-rolls of single shots
Any kind of brand kit, asset library or team review flow
moatNotes: The interesting engineering is upstream in the video models and the GPU bill, not in the product surface you actually touch.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative is assembling four API vendors, eating the per-second inference cost yourself, and still ending up with output that looks a generation behind. Products like this are buying you a curated pipeline and a set of defaults that make the result watchable, which is most of the value in generative video. The moment you want twenty variants of a thirty second ad by Thursday, the subscription is cheaper than your weekend.
notes: The timeline renderer is a weekend; the video model is not. The moat is model access plus the GPU capacity to serve it, and the taste baked into the default templates.
prompt:
Build a local CLI tool called reelsmith that renders vertical short-form videos from a script. No web app, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud storage.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Node 20 with TypeScript, run via tsx
- ffmpeg and ffprobe invoked as child processes, assume they are on PATH
- commander for the CLI, zod for config validation
- No database, everything is files on disk

Commands:
- reelsmith init: writes reel.config.json and a .env.example
- reelsmith script "topic": calls an LLM to produce a JSON script of 5 to 8 beats, each beat with narration text and a short visual description, saved to project/script.json
- reelsmith voice: sends each beat's narration to a TTS API, saves per-beat WAV files, runs ffprobe to record exact durations back into script.json
- reelsmith build: assembles the video
- reelsmith preview: builds at 480p with a fast preset

Build behavior:
- Read clips from project/media, matched to beats by filename prefix (01-, 02-). If a beat has no clip, fall back to a solid color card with the visual description as placeholder text.
- Scale and center-crop every clip to 1080x1920, trim or loop it to match that beat's audio duration
- Concatenate beats with the concat demuxer, mix in project/media/music.mp3 at -18dB if present, duck nothing, keep it simple
- Burn in captions from the narration text using drawtext, word-wrapped, bottom third, bundled font in assets/
- Output project/out/reel.mp4, H.264 yuv420p, faststart

Rules:
- OPENAI_API_KEY and TTS_API_KEY come from .env, never hardcoded, never logged
- If a key is missing, fail with a clear message naming the env var
- Deterministic: same script.json and same media means byte-identical output where ffmpeg allows
- Explicitly out of scope: text-to-video generation, avatars, lipsync, stock footage search, publishing to any platform

Include a README with install steps, the ffmpeg requirement, and one worked example project checked into examples/.
